samples.summary: `openBrowser`'s new async-error absorption is fully mocked away — no test can fail if it regresses
samples.evidence: The whole point of the new `openBrowser` helper is that `open()` resolves on spawn and the failure arrives later as an async `error` event on the child (`child?.on?.('error', () => {})`, login.ts:180), which unhandled kills the process. The only test file that drives `login` (`packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:15`) mocks the module wholesale: `vi.mock('open', () => ({ default: vi.fn(async () => undefined) }))`, so `child` is always `undefined` and the `.on('error')` registration is never exercised. There is no test anywhere that returns a child emitting `error`, nor one where the dynamic `import('open')` rejects. Deleting the `child?.on?.(...)` line leaves every test green.

samples.summary: The new `command: commandPath(this)` plumbing into the import/upload/download orchestrators has no test at any of those five call sites
samples.evidence: `runFilesUpload`, `runFilesDownload`, `runDocsImport`, `runNotesImport` and `runSlidesImport` all gained a `command` arg that is stamped into their error envelopes, and each action now passes `commandPath(this)`. Grepping `command:` across packages/cli/test finds it only in login-callback.test.ts, ctx.test.ts and output.test.ts (unit-level `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`, `docs.content`, `docs.get`, `schema`). The existing orchestrator suites (files-upload.test.ts, files-download.test.ts, docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts) call the run* functions without `command` and never assert the field, so dropping `command: commandPath(this)` from any of the five actions is undetectable.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`: the TTY branch, the 0o600 file mode, and the failure fallback are untested
samples.evidence: Only the non-TTY file branch is exercised (login-callback.test.ts:178-179 asserts the path is mentioned and the file contents). Nothing asserts `statSync(urlPath).mode & 0o777 === 0o600`, even though the test comment claims 'in a file only its owner can read' — the security property the code documents (login.ts:215) is not asserted. The TTY branch (login.ts:200-207, prints the URL) and the catch fallback (login.ts:222-229) have no test at all.

samples.summary: The login-URL assertions depend on the ambient `process.stderr.isTTY`, so they assert nothing deterministic
samples.evidence: `announceLoginUrl` branches on `process.stderr.isTTY`, and the test never stubs it. Under a TTY (vitest run interactively) the command takes the print branch, so `notices.some(n => n.includes('nonce='))` becomes true and `expect(...).toBe(false)` fails; the file at `urlPath` is never written. The test's central claim ('nothing carrying the nonce reaches stderr') is therefore an assertion about the CI environment rather than about the code.

samples.summary: The new `sawUnboundCode` timeout message has no test
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` now records `sawUnboundCode` when a callback arrives with no `state` (login.ts:332) and swaps in a distinct timeout error (login.ts:388-392). login-callback.test.ts only checks the 400 responses; no test uses fake timers or drives the 30s timeout, so both branches of that ternary are uncovered and the flag could be inverted or dropped silently.

samples.summary: `logSafeUrl` is unit-tested but its wiring into the pino `req` serializer is not
samples.evidence: log-safe-url.spec.ts covers the function thoroughly, but no test asserts the app.module serializer actually calls it — reverting `url: logSafeUrl(req.url)` back to `url: req.url` leaves the whole backend suite green while re-exposing `/auth` query secrets in access logs, which is the stated purpose of the change.

github-auth.guard.spec.ts always supplies a response object with a `cookie` function (spec:25-28), so the guard's explicit guard clause `if (typeof res?.cookie !== 'function') throw new InternalServerErrorException(...)` is never reached by any test.

samples.summary: The controller's CLI port-range re-check has no test
samples.evidence: `if (port < 1024 || port > 65535) throw new BadRequestException('Invalid CLI port')` in `githubAuthCallback` is reachable only via a state entry with an out-of-range port; `startCliLogin` in auth.controller.spec.ts accepts a `port` override but no test ever passes an invalid one, so this defence-in-depth branch is uncovered (the guard-level check is covered separately).

login-callback.test.ts covers 401 → UNAUTHORIZED/exit 2 and 502 → SYSTEM/exit 2, but no test drives a 4xx other than 401/403 (e.g. 400), so the `HTTP_ERROR` branch and its distinct exit code 1 in `failFromBackend` (login.ts:270) are never exercised.

finding.summary: `openBrowser`'s new async-error absorption is fully mocked away — no test can fail if it regresses

The only test file that drives `login` (`packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:15`) mocks the module wholesale: `vi.mock('open', () => ({ default: vi.fn(async () => undefined) }))`, so `child` is always `undefined` and the `.on('error')` registration is never exercised. verdict.reason: Verified independently. login.ts:176-184 registers an async 'error' handler on the child returned by open(). The sole test that drives the login command mocks the module wholesale with `vi.mock('open', () => ({ default: vi.fn(async () => undefined) }))` (login-callback.test.ts:17), so `child` is always undefined and the optional-chained `.on('error')` at login.ts:180 is never executed; the mock exists only to read the authorization URL (test:88-93). Repo-wide greps for `from 'open'` / `import('open')` / `require('open')` return only login.ts:178 and that one test; greps for importers of `commands/login` return only src/cli.ts:10 and that same test. vitest.config.ts:5 limits discovery to `test/**/*.test.ts`, and no e2e suite or CI workflow runs the login flow. No test returns a child emitting 'error' and none makes the dynamic import reject, so removing login.ts:180 (or the catch) leaves every test green. Real, in-lane missing coverage for a behavior change; no counterexample found.

searchedFor: grep for 'app.module' in backend spec files
finding.summary: New `/auth` log-redaction helper `logSafeUrl` has no test at all (and is unexported, so it cannot be tested)
finding.evidence: `logSafeUrl` implements a security-motivated behavior (replace the query string of any `/auth` URL with `?<redacted>`, keep the query elsewhere) with a non-trivial regex `/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` and a non-string passthrough. There is no `packages/backend/src/app.module.spec.ts` (Glob over `packages/backend/src/**/*.spec.ts` lists none) and a repo-wide grep for `logSafeUrl` returns only app.module.ts:34/87 plus a prose mention in docs/design/rest-api.md:396. Nothing exercises the boundary cases the comment claims (`/authors?x=1` must NOT be redacted; `/auth` with no query; a non-string url). The function is also module-private, so a regression here is invisible to every lane.

verdict.reason: The finding's premises do not hold in this repository. `logSafeUrl` is not an unexported helper inside `app.module.ts`: it lives in its own module at packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts:38 and is exported (`export function logSafeUrl`), imported by app.module.ts:23 and used at app.module.ts:70. A dedicated spec exists at packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.spec.ts and it covers precisely the boundary cases the reviewer says nothing exercises: a non-`/auth` prefix is NOT redacted (:43 `/authz?token=t` unchanged, :44 `/api/v1/auth?x=1` unchanged — same class as the reviewer's `/authors?x=1`), `/auth` with no query passes through (:48), and non-string urls pass through (:54-56 undefined/null/42). It additionally covers case-insensitive, percent-encoded and double-slash spellings (:28-37) and a malformed percent escape (:62), matching the normalization in log-safe-url.ts:12-23. The tests import the real function (no mocking) and assert concrete expected output strings, so they fail if the regex or passthrough logic regresses — not vacuous. The spec is genuinely executed: packages/backend/package.json:106-107 sets rootDir "src" and testRegex ".*\\.spec\\.ts$", which matches src/logging/log-safe-url.spec.ts. The reviewer searched only for app.module.spec.ts and so missed the extracted module.

finding.summary: The renamed `__cliStateToken` → `__oauthState` handoff from guard to strategy is not covered by any test
finding.evidence: `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` now reads `req.__oauthState` and copies it into `opts.state`; `github-auth.guard.ts:111,116` is the only writer. github.strategy.spec.ts only asserts endpoint URLs — it never calls `authenticate` or inspects `opts.state`. A grep for `__oauthState`/`__cliStateToken` across packages/backend finds matches only in the guard, the guard spec, the strategy source and a controller comment — no test asserts the strategy forwards it. If the two ever disagree (a half-applied rename), the authorization request would reach GitHub with no `state` at all (passport-oauth2's NullStore always verifies), i.e. no CSRF binding, and the whole backend suite would still be green.

verdict.reason: The claim that no test covers the `__oauthState` guard→strategy handoff is factually wrong in this tree. `github.strategy.spec.ts:129-183` is a dedicated `describe('GitHubStrategy state injection')` block that calls `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` directly with `{ __oauthState: ... }` on the request and inspects the options passed to `super.authenticate` (stubbed on the mixin prototype that `super` resolves to, per github.strategy.ts:67). It asserts: state forwarded for the browser `w.`-prefixed half (line 161-164), CLI token forwarded unchanged (line 169), no `state` key emitted when the guard set none — with `expect(seen).toBeDefined()` first so the stub is provably invoked (lines 174-175), and that the caller's options object is not mutated (line 181). A half-applied rename (strategy still reading `__cliStateToken`) would leave `seen.state` undefined and fail lines 163 and 169. Only passport-oauth2's own `authenticate` is stubbed — the logic under test (github.strategy.ts:61-68) runs for real, so this is not over-mocking. The guard-side writer is separately asserted against the same literal key at github-auth.guard.spec.ts:66,160,196,218,231. The reviewer's grep result is also refuted: matches exist in github.strategy.spec.ts at lines 123, 157, 168, 180.
